status: Contextual research leads only; MIRCO is not identified and no ciphertext repair is justified by geography
observed_cipher_constraint: The A4 conditional editorial reading retains MIRCO. Its full version already requires nine known-coordinate substitutions and thirteen erasure fillings; those edits are independently itemized in data/certificates/p164_A4_editorial.json.

primary_sources.author: Léonce Martin
primary_sources.title: En campagne européenne 1914-1919: 1er régiment de chasseurs d’Afrique
primary_sources.publisher: Imprimerie militaire Charles-Lavauzelle, Paris and Limoges
primary_sources.scan_provenance: The PDF identifies Bibliothèque nationale de France / Gallica and Service historique de la Défense on its cover. Retrieved from a public mirror.

findings.statement: The author identifies a German post at Mosnac as twenty men of the 4th Squadron, 1st Prussian Dragoons, with the parenthetical name Kaiserin-Victoria.
findings.implication: This independently associates a closely matching cavalry unit designation with the Danube sector immediately before the Miroc episode. It does not locate the unit on 9 November or prove the German message expansion.

findings.statement: The account describes French movements between Mosnac, Mianovac and Miroc, a failed German counterattack in wooded ground southwest of Miroc, and a French withdrawal to Jabukovac.
findings.implication: A near-contemporary regimental narrative places fighting around the similarly named Miroc; no exact match to the A4 report is established.

findings.statement: The narrative says a German brigade with two squadrons of the 11th Hussars held the Miroc-Milainovac line and patrolled against the French until 11 November, when it crossed the Danube.
findings.implication: This creates chronological tension with identifying the 9 November A4 occupation report as this specific locality. A line of positions, a village, and a transient report need not describe identical control, so it is a counterpoint rather than a formal contradiction.

primary_sources.author: United States War Department
primary_sources.title: Histories of Two Hundred and Fifty-One Divisions of the German Army Which Participated in the War (1914-1918)
primary_sources.statement: The 218th Division order-of-battle table lists the 4th Squadron of the 1st Guard Dragoon Regiment in its 1917 column; the 1918 column lists the 4th Squadron of the 1st Dragoon Regiment, omitting Guard.
primary_sources.limit: An order of battle is not a direct record of the squadron location or report on 9 November.

bounded_archive_search.result: No persuasive parallel to the p164 message was identified in the retrieved hits. General reports concern troops and transport around Osijek and Vinkovci.
bounded_archive_search.limit: This is an OCR-assisted and selectively visually checked search. It does not claim exhaustive visual review or prove absence of a parallel.

spelling_counterfactual.status: Diagnostic only; not an adopted repair
spelling_counterfactual.change: Replace both editorial MIRCO occurrences in A4 by MIROC
spelling_counterfactual.meaning: A geographical identification cannot be implemented as a source-preserving spelling normalization. Keeping the source reading MIRCO while discussing Miroc as a possibility avoids silently changing cipher evidence.

unresolved: Whether MIRCO names a geographic locality, a station, an operational name, or a malformed spelling.
Whether Martin’s 1st Prussian Dragoons label denotes exactly the same formation as the editorial expansion of 4./1. G. DRAG.
Whether any surviving German or French daily record repeats the actual 9 November message.
not_adopted: ESSEK as proof of Osijek: the letter sequence can be internal to ABGESESSENEN.
A literal Prince Mirko interpretation of MIRCO.
Height 828 as an anchor for selecting a locality.
Any claim that the Martin narrative cryptographically proves the A4 repairs.

uninspected_primary_lead.status: The date range and reference are attested in the official inventory; the daily manuscript entries were not inspected.
uninspected_primary_lead.access_attempt: The public Mémoire des hommes catalogue timed out in web retrieval and a separate ordinary HTTP request. No daily-entry conclusion is drawn.
